title: N11 claimed folded but the retry budget is dead code — GALLERY_MAX_RETRIES does not exist, `retries` is never read, and the gallery stage machine still retries forever
evidence: app/gallery.odin:57: `retries:  int, // N11: the condition-poll frame budget (GALLERY_MAX_RETRIES)` — repo-wide grep for `retries` returns exactly this one line; `GALLERY_MAX_RETRIES` has zero definitions. The retry arms re-arm unbounded: `.Draw_Release:` `gallery.wait = 5 // the commit lands via the executor — poll` `return false`; `.Noc:` `gallery.wait = 5` `return false`; `.Deselect:` `gallery.wait = 5 // the ESC deselect lands via the intent chain` `return false`; `.Settings:` `gallery.wait = 5` `return false` — no frame/stage counter is consulted anywhere in gallery_frame. Commit b4154c3 title: `fix: Perkins r1 — B1 fail-loud loader (report, never coerce), B2 PR body rewrite, + W1-W5, N1-N15`
detail: The fix commit claims N1–N15 folded, but N11's fold is a comment plus a never-read field naming a constant that was never written. The unbounded-retry condition r1 flagged stands unchanged; a claimed-but-absent fix defeats the audit.
recommended_fix: Define GALLERY_MAX_RETRIES, increment retries on every condition-poll re-arm (reset per stage), and abort the run with the stage name when the budget is exceeded.

title: Audio seam refactor dropped rl.CloseAudioDevice() entirely — the device is never closed on normal builds and audio_destroy's comment now states the opposite
evidence: app/audio/audio.odin:316: `// audio_destroy — unload the sounds + close the device (app teardown).` — the proc body ends after `audio_stop_music(a.bed)` / `audio_unload_music(a.bed)` with no close call; repo-wide grep for `CloseAudioDevice` across app/, harness/, core/ returns zero hits; the 17-wrapper seam (verified: 17 `:: proc` pairs in the when/else blocks) has no `audio_close_device`. raylib 6.0 raudio.c defines CloseAudioDevice (line 531) with no atexit auto-close, and rcore.c CloseWindow never touches audio.
detail: The refactor needed the call gone for raudio-less SW builds but added no wrapper, so normal builds lost the teardown call too — a behavior change in #86's teardown idiom the rebase was required to preserve. Impact is exit-time only (single deferred call at process end).
recommended_fix: Add an 18th wrapper: audio_close_device (no-op under PP_SW_AUDIO, rl.CloseAudioDevice() otherwise); call it at the end of audio_destroy and fix the stale comment.

title: font_test data-stage probes never free the glyph arrays or recs — only the atlas image is unloaded, so the new fail-loud loader's MemFree discipline is incomplete on the test side
evidence: font_probe_warning: `glyphs, count := font_merge_fallback(main_path, fallback_path, FONT_BASE_SIZE, cps[:])` — glyphs (rl.MemAlloc'd merged block + per-glyph image data) never freed before return. font_guard_reports_missing_asset: `_, _, ok := font_atlas_build_from_file(FONT_ASSET)` — all three results (font with glyphs+recs, atlas image) discarded with no unload on the success case. font_mono_tabular_digits: `defer rl.UnloadImage(am)` / `defer rl.UnloadImage(ab)` — frees the atlas pixels only; mono.glyphs/body.glyphs (MemAlloc) and mono.recs/body.recs (raylib RL_MALLOC inside GenImageFontAtlas) leak.
detail: App/harness paths are sound (font blocks owned by the Font, freed at process teardown), but each test run leaks the merged glyph arrays and recs via raylib's C allocator — invisible to Odin's leak tracker. Test-process-lifetime only, few KB per run.
recommended_fix: Free after the assertions: rl.UnloadFontData(glyphs, count) + rl.MemFree(f.recs) (or an unload helper in view.odin), at least in font_probe_warning which loads twice per negative-control run.
